items.title: NVIDIA and Meta to Expand Collaboration on Muse and Muse Family of Models Amid Robust Growth
items.summary: NVIDIA and Meta announced an expanded partnership to optimize infrastructure for AI agents, particularly Meta's Muse models. Meta will deploy NVIDIA's Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X networking, and BlueField-4 technology. NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering. The collaboration aims to improve inference and training performance while enhancing security and monitoring capabilities for AI agent deployment.

items.title: AMD Has a Credible Path to Challenge Its Biggest Competitor But There's a Catch
items.summary: AMD is building a comprehensive AI platform combining GPUs, CPUs, networking, and software to compete in the data center market. While the opportunity is significant and backed by major tech companies, success depends on customer repeat deployments, ROCm software adoption, margin expansion, and free cash flow generation.

items.title: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan Has Incredible News for AMD Stock Investors
items.summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan revealed that the company can only meet 50% of customer demand for server CPUs, indicating a significant supply shortage. While this benefits both Intel and AMD through potential price increases, AMD is positioned as the bigger beneficiary due to its superior technology, growing market share (34.5% vs Intel's declining share), and ability to ramp production with TSMC. AMD's data center revenue grew 107% year-over-year in Q2, and the company expects 80%+ growth in server revenue for H2 2026, compared to Intel's slowing growth trajectory.

items.title: Is Arm Holdings Still a Hidden Winner of the AI Chip Race?
items.summary: Arm Holdings, which licenses CPU designs rather than manufacturing chips, is positioned as a crucial but underappreciated player in the AI infrastructure boom. The company collects royalties on every unit shipped and is expanding beyond smartphones into data centers, where major tech companies like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Nvidia build Arm-based CPUs. With recent revenue growth of 23-24% and higher royalty rates from newer architectures, Arm has outperformed Nvidia over the past three years, though its valuation at 55x sales remains richly priced.
